proposals.before: Tang put on a show of surprise. "Almost certainly some old enemy of Li Wen," he said.
proposals.after: Tang put on a show of surprise. "Almost certainly some old acquaintance of Li Wen who bore him a grudge," he said.
proposals.reason: 文故人 means an old acquaintance of Li Wen who resented him, not an established old enemy.

proposals.before: Another attendant forced himself on a palace maidservant; her brother laid a complaint. Anshi said, "The girl is a bondservant venting spite—she slanders a man who wears official cap and gown."
proposals.after: Another attendant had illicit relations with a palace maidservant; her brother lodged a complaint. Anshi said, "The slave, out of resentment, is falsely smearing an official."
proposals.reason: 淫 does not by itself state coercion, and 奴 in Anshi's reply refers to the accusing slave (the maidservant's brother), not to the girl.

proposals.before: He had the girl reassigned as a punishment slave.
proposals.after: He instructed the office to punish the accusing slave.
proposals.reason: The girl was already an official maidservant; 告署適奴 (適 read 謫) directs punishment at the slave who made the accusation, not reassignment of the girl.

proposals.before: He reported and marked him fit for slave.
proposals.after: He notified the office and had the slave punished.
proposals.reason: 適 is read 謫, 'to punish or censure'; the original literal rendering misreads the phrase as assigning slave status.

proposals.before: Seeing how exalted he and his father had become, Anshi grew uneasy. He asked that his son Yanshou be given a provincial post, and the emperor appointed Yanshou governor of Beidi.
proposals.after: Seeing how exalted he and his son had become, Anshi grew uneasy. He asked that his son Yanshou be given a provincial post, and the emperor appointed Yanshou governor of Beidi.
proposals.reason: 父子 here denotes Anshi and his son Yanshou; 'he and his father' reverses the generation identified in the following clause.

proposals.before: Soon after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, an edict ordered the ranked marquises to recommend men of outstanding talent. Xiao Bo recommended Chen Tang, assistant director of the imperial kitchen.
proposals.after: Soon after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, an edict ordered the ranked marquises to recommend men of outstanding talent. Zhang Bo recommended Chen Tang, assistant director of the imperial kitchen.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the recommender only as 勃, Zhang Bo's given name; “Xiao Bo” invents a surname and misidentifies him.

proposals.before: He kept his title even under Wang Mang, and in the Jianwu era rose step by step to grand minister of works; Guangwudi carved a detached village out of the old Fuping fief and re-enfeoffed him as marquis of Wushi.
proposals.after: He kept his title even under Wang Mang, and in the Jianwu era rose step by step to grand minister of works; he was re-enfeoffed with a detached village of Fuping as marquis of Wushi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 更封富平之別鄉為武始侯 does not name Guangwudi; the idiomatic English invents an imperial agent absent from the source.

proposals.before: The Zhangs had begun at Duling. Zhang Anshi's household moved with each imperial tomb town under Wudi, Zhaodi, and Xuandi—three relocations in all—before returning to Duling.
proposals.after: Zhang Tang originally lived at Duling. Under Wudi, Zhaodi, and Xuandi, Anshi always moved with the mausoleum towns—three relocations in all—before returning to Duling.
proposals.reason: Chinese begins 張湯本居杜陵, naming Zhang Tang personally; idiomatic replaces him with the collective 'The Zhangs', omitting the named individual.

proposals.before: The quiet kindness Zhang He once showed the future Emperor Xuan also played its part in the family's lasting good fortune.
proposals.after: Zhang He's hidden virtue also played its part.
proposals.reason: Chinese 賀之陰德，亦有助云 does not mention Emperor Xuan or spell out the kindness's recipient; idiomatic invents that detail.

proposals.before: A gentleman violated a palace slave girl; the girl's elder brother spoke for himself; Anshi said, "The slave in resentment and anger falsely defiled cap and robe."
proposals.after: A gentleman-attendant had illicit relations with a palace maid. Her elder brother lodged a complaint. Anshi said, "The slave, out of resentment and anger, falsely smeared an official."
proposals.reason: 淫 does not establish coercion, 婢兄自言 is the maid's brother lodging the complaint, and 衣冠 denotes an official; the revision corrects all three references.

decisions.after: Tang put on a show of surprise. "Probably one of Wen's old acquaintances with a grudge against him," he said.
decisions.reason: 文故人怨之 means an old acquaintance of Wen who bore him a grudge; the revision restores both ideas in natural dialogue.

decisions.after: A gentleman-attendant had illicit relations with a palace maid. Her brother lodged a complaint. Anshi said, "The slave is acting out of resentment and falsely smearing an official."
decisions.reason: 淫 does not establish coercion, and after 婢兄自言 the 奴 Anshi blames is the accusing brother, not the maidservant; the revision keeps those references clear.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 婢兄自言，安世曰：「奴以恚怒，誣污衣冠。」

decisions.after: He ordered the office to punish the accusing slave.
decisions.reason: 告署適奴, with 適 read as 謫, has Anshi order the office to punish the accusing slave; the palace maid was already 官婢 and is not reassigned here.
With 適 read 謫, the literal sense is notifying the office and punishing the slave, not marking someone fit for slave status.
安世自見父子尊顯 followed by 為子延壽 identifies the exalted pair as Anshi and his son, not Anshi and his father.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安世自見父子尊顯……為子延壽求出補吏

decisions.reason: Preceding 子勃嗣 identifies 勃 as Zhang Bo; “Xiao Bo” invents a surname absent from the Chinese.
更封富平之別鄉為武始侯 is a passive re-enfeoffment in the Jianwu era; Guangwudi is not named as the agent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 更封富平之別鄉為武始侯

decisions.after: Zhang Tang originally lived at Duling. During the reigns of Emperor Wu, Emperor Zhao, and Emperor Xuan, Anshi followed each new imperial mausoleum settlement—three relocations in all—before returning to Duling.
decisions.reason: 張湯本居杜陵 names Zhang Tang personally, while 安世 is the subject of the three subsequent mausoleum-town relocations; the revision restores both subjects clearly.

The existing sentence naturally explains 賀之陰德 by reference to Zhang He's earlier protection of the future Emperor Xuan; that contextual clarification is accurate and preferable to the opaque phrase 'hidden virtue.'
淫 does not establish coercion, 婢兄自言 is the maid's brother lodging the complaint, and 衣冠 denotes an official; the revision corrects all three references.
